subject: Nanotechnology
title: Toxicity and Biocompatibility
description: A fast breakdown of Toxicity and Biocompatibility for builders.

hook.text: A material safe in bulk can become toxic as a nanoparticle — size changes everything, including danger.

buildup.text: Nanoparticles can generate reactive oxygen species inside cells — damaging DNA, proteins, and membranes.

discovery.text: Toxicity depends on composition, size, shape, surface charge, and dose — each must be tested individually.

twist.text: Standard toxicity tests designed for chemicals often fail for nanoparticles — they need nano-specific protocols.

climax.text: The FDA now requires nano-specific safety data — driving a new field called nanotoxicology.

punchline.text: Safe in bulk does not mean safe at nanoscale — size rewrites toxicity.

quiz.question: Why can nanomaterials be toxic even when the bulk material is safe?
options: High surface area increases reactivity and they can enter cells and generate reactive oxygen species
They become radioactive at small sizes
